name: Sushi
tagline: Vinegared rice topped with fresh seafood
summary: Bite-size vinegared rice topped with raw or lightly cooked fish and shellfish. Conveyor-belt sushi bars are cheap and fun, while counter-style restaurants serve an omakase (chef's choice) course. Many regions also have their own pressed or leaf-wrapped sushi.

name: Sashimi
tagline: Thinly sliced raw fish
summary: Slices of very fresh raw fish served with soy sauce and wasabi, without rice. Coastal towns each have their own prized catch, such as seared bonito in Kochi and premium horse mackerel in Oita.

name: Ramen
tagline: Noodles in a rich, savory broth
summary: Wheat noodles in a hot broth, usually flavored with soy sauce, salt, miso or pork bone (tonkotsu), and topped with sliced pork, egg and green onion. Almost every region has its own style, which makes ramen one of the best ways to taste local food.

name: Tempura
tagline: Light, crispy battered seafood and vegetables
summary: Shrimp, fish and seasonal vegetables coated in a thin batter and deep-fried until light and crispy. It is dipped in a light broth or sprinkled with salt, and is also served on rice as tendon.

name: Soba
tagline: Buckwheat noodles, hot or cold
summary: Thin noodles made from buckwheat flour, eaten cold with a dipping sauce or hot in broth. Mountain areas with cool climates are famous for fragrant handmade soba.

name: Udon
tagline: Thick, chewy wheat noodles
summary: Thick wheat noodles with a soft, chewy texture, served in a mild broth or with a dipping sauce. Kagawa is known as the home of udon, and other regions have thin, flat or miso-simmered versions.

name: Tonkatsu
tagline: Crispy breaded pork cutlet
summary: A thick pork cutlet coated in panko breadcrumbs and deep-fried, served with shredded cabbage, rice, miso soup and a thick, fruity sauce. Regional versions use miso sauce or come on rice as katsudon.

name: Yakitori
tagline: Grilled chicken skewers
summary: Bite-size pieces of chicken grilled on skewers over charcoal and seasoned with salt or a sweet soy glaze. It is a classic at izakaya (Japanese pubs) and goes well with beer.

name: Okonomiyaki
tagline: Savory pancake cooked on a griddle
summary: A savory pancake of batter, cabbage and pork or seafood, cooked on a hot iron griddle and topped with sauce, mayonnaise and bonito flakes. Osaka mixes everything together, while Hiroshima layers it with noodles.

name: Takoyaki
tagline: Octopus balls from Osaka
summary: Round balls of batter with a piece of octopus inside, cooked in a special molded pan and topped with sauce, mayonnaise and bonito flakes. Crispy outside and soft inside, it is Osaka's favorite street food.

name: Gyoza
tagline: Pan-fried dumplings
summary: Thin dumplings filled with minced pork, cabbage and garlic, pan-fried until crispy on the bottom. Utsunomiya and Hamamatsu compete for the title of Japan's gyoza capital.

name: Nikuman (steamed buns)
tagline: Fluffy steamed buns with a savory filling
summary: Soft, fluffy steamed buns filled with juicy minced pork and onion. Sold hot at convenience stores in winter, and in Chinatowns and specialty shops all year round. Fun variations include pizza buns with tomato sauce and cheese, and seafood or curry fillings.

name: Japanese curry
tagline: Mild, thick curry on rice
summary: A thick, mildly spiced curry with meat and vegetables served over rice, often with a pork cutlet on top. It is one of Japan's most popular everyday meals, and several cities have their own distinctive style.

name: Sukiyaki
tagline: Beef simmered in a sweet soy broth
summary: Thin slices of beef, tofu and vegetables simmered at the table in a sweet soy sauce broth, then dipped in raw egg. It is a special-occasion dish, best with famous wagyu beef.

name: Shabu-shabu
tagline: Hot pot of thinly sliced meat
summary: Paper-thin slices of meat or fish swished through a pot of hot broth at the table, then dipped in sesame or ponzu sauce. Light and healthy, it shows off the quality of the ingredients.

name: Oden
tagline: Hearty one-pot stew, perfect in winter
summary: Daikon radish, boiled eggs, fish cakes, konjac and tofu simmered for hours in a light dashi broth and eaten with a dab of mustard. You can pick pieces one by one at convenience stores, food stalls and izakaya, and the broth and toppings change from region to region.

name: Donburi (rice bowls)
tagline: Toppings served on a bowl of rice
summary: A big bowl of rice with toppings such as beef (gyudon), chicken and egg (oyakodon), cutlet (katsudon) or fresh seafood (kaisendon). Quick, filling and good value, it is a favorite lunch in Japan.

name: Onigiri
tagline: Rice balls for a quick bite
summary: Rice shaped into a triangle or ball, often wrapped in seaweed and filled with salmon, pickled plum or tuna mayo. You can find them in every convenience store, and some regions have their own unique versions.

regional.ja: ポークたまごおにぎり

name: Unagi (grilled eel)
tagline: Eel grilled with a sweet soy glaze
summary: Freshwater eel grilled over charcoal and brushed with a sweet soy sauce glaze, served on rice. It is rich and tender, and Nagoya's hitsumabushi lets you enjoy it three different ways.

regional.ja: 柳川うなぎのせいろ蒸し

name: Wagyu beef
tagline: Japan's famous marbled beef
summary: Japanese beef known for its fine marbling and melt-in-the-mouth texture. Each region raises its own brand of wagyu, enjoyed as steak, sukiyaki or yakiniku (grilled meat).

name: Yakiniku (Japanese BBQ)
tagline: Grill your own meat at the table
summary: Bite-size cuts of beef and pork that you grill yourself over a charcoal or gas grill at the table, then dip in a sweet soy-based sauce. Restaurants range from cheap all-you-can-eat places to high-end wagyu specialists. Some regions grill lamb or chicken instead.

name: Horumon (grilled offal)
tagline: Chewy, flavorful grilled offal
summary: Beef or pork offal such as intestine, tripe and heart, grilled over a fire and dipped in a garlicky miso or soy sauce. It is cheap, full of flavor and a favorite with locals at casual grill restaurants. Some towns even stir-fry it with noodles.

regional.ja: 厚木シロコロ・ホルモン

name: Yakisoba
tagline: Stir-fried noodles with sauce
summary: Wheat noodles stir-fried with cabbage and pork in a tangy sauce, a staple at festivals and street stalls. Several towns are famous for their own local style.

name: Wagashi & matcha sweets
ja: 和菓子・抹茶スイーツ
tagline: Traditional Japanese sweets
summary: Traditional sweets made from rice, sweet red bean paste and seasonal ingredients, often enjoyed with green tea. Kyoto is the place to try elegant wagashi and rich matcha desserts.
